messages:
Maria Chen: Quick follow-up to the RFC — I'd like to propose we add an explicit sticky session header for streaming requests so transient retries land on the same backend and can reuse the KV/prefix cache. Idea: `X-Stream-Session: <uuid>` + optional `X-Resume-Token` in trailers. Keeps progress visible and avoids re-computation on short retries.

Devon K: curious — does this assume requests are idempotent? what about side-effects mid-stream? :thinking:

Maria Chen: good call. we only sticky for read-only or non-committal paths (generation/embeddings). for calls with side-effects we'd refuse to sticky and route through a non-resumable path. leave config toggle at route-level.

Suraj P: operational question — how do we bound the session lifetime? infinite sticky sessions = hot partitions. propose TTL + lease refresh from backend when active. also need a way to signal invalidation on backend restart.

Adam L: fallback story: if backend dies mid-stream and token can't be recovered, we should fallback to fast stateless replica (smaller model) with a clear progress indicator to client. better than forcing full restart.

Lina R: observability: we need per-session tracing and progress metrics. attach trace/span id to header and emit periodic progress trailers so Console can show percent-complete. also cost accounting per session.

Devon K: tiny proto for header usage: 

```
GET /v1/stream/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.dev
Authorization: Bearer <token>
X-Stream-Session: 123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000
X-Trace-Id: 01abc...
```

Backend responses can include `Trailer: X-Resume-Token` and send `X-Resume-Token: <opaque>` as a final trailer.

OpsBot: metric note — sticky sessions increase median CPU per host when hot. simulate with 10k synthetic sessions before commit. :robot_face:

Maria Chen: agreed on simulation. implementation sketch: router picks backend by consistent-hash(session-id) OR by last-known binding stored in short-lived in-memory map with soft-eviction. consistent-hash means easier failover but harder to rebalance. map + lease easier to move.

David H: tradeoff: consistent-hash => stable cache locality but rebalancing causes large cache churn. map+lease => central coordination to keep binding; adds control-plane ops. maybe hybrid: consistent-hash for initial placement + ephemeral map for overrides.

Suraj P: security: resume tokens must be opaque and encrypted per-tenant to avoid cross-tenant leak if misrouted. token TTL + rotation. also ensure we don't leak model state in token.

Lina R: UX: clients should get progress trailers like `X-Progress: 43%` and a resume hint. For streaming SDKs we can expose a `resume()` method that takes resume-token.

Adam L: test matrix we need: backend restart mid-session, long-tail sticky sessions with churn, tenant isolation failure injection, and cost regression under high stickiness.

Maria Chen: next steps: I'll draft an RFC with these sections: header format, session lifecycle (TTL/lease/renewal), routing algorithm options, fallback semantics, observability, security. Can people volunteer to review?

Devon K: happy to review.

Suraj P: I'll take ops/runbook + test plans.

Lina R: I'll write observability + SDK hooks.

David H: I'll do routing algorithm and perf sims.

Adam L: I'll draft fallback and client UX suggestions.

Maria Chen: thanks — I'll post the RFC this week. :+1:

Adam L: quick question — do we want a server-side API to forcibly detach a sticky session (admin kill)? would help debugging.

Maria Chen: yes — admin `POST /admin/sessions/{id}/invalidate` with audit log. Ops-only.

OpsBot: note added: create synthetic load job `sticky-sim-v1` in perf infra.

Lina R: tiny nit — prefer `X-Stream-Session` be lowercase-friendly in proxies (`x-stream-session`) for nginx/forwarding. doc should mention canonical header name and lowercase handling.

Maria Chen: noted. final: RFC will include sample SDK snippets, header canonicalization guidance, and migration plan (opt-in routes first). ping me if you want to be a co-author.

Devon K: :wave: thanks, looking forward to the RFC.

Suraj P: :+1:
